holidays.name: National Sea Serpent Day
holidays.description: A day for sea monster fans. Look out over the waves, swap legends of giant serpents rising from the deep, and keep an open mind about what might be down there.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It builds on centuries of sailors' tales and sea serpent sightings from around the world.
holidays.funFact: Old maps often drew sea serpents in the margins of the ocean. Some of those sightings may have been oarfish, which can grow longer than 30 feet.

holidays.name: National Raspberries and Cream Day
holidays.description: A day for one of the simplest desserts there is: plump, tart raspberries with smooth, sweet cream. You can serve them in a bowl, over shortcake, or in a parfait.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It falls in peak raspberry season, which makes it a good time to eat them.
holidays.funFact: A raspberry isn't a single berry. It's a cluster of tiny fruits called drupelets, and each one has its own seed.

holidays.name: National Lighthouse Day
holidays.description: A salute to the towers that guided ships safely past rocky shores. Visit a lighthouse, climb its spiral stairs, or just enjoy the view.
holidays.origin: The date marks August 7, 1789. On that day the U.S. Congress passed an act that put lighthouses under federal government control.
holidays.funFact: The Lighthouse Act of 1789 was one of the first public works laws passed by the new U.S. Congress.
